config_entry_only.description:
The {domain} integration does not support configuration via YAML file. You may not notice any obvious issues with the integration, but any configuration settings defined in YAML are not actually applied.

To resolve this:

1. If you've not already done so, [set up the integration]({add_integration}).

2. Remove `{domain}:` from your YAML configuration file.

3. Restart Home Assistant.
config_entry_only.title: The {domain} integration does not support YAML configuration

config_entry_unique_id_collision.description:
There are multiple {domain} config entries with the same unique ID.
The config entries are named {titles}.

To fix this error, [configure the integration]({configure_url}) and remove all except one of the duplicates.

Note: Another group of duplicates may be revealed after removing these duplicates.
config_entry_unique_id_collision.title: Multiple {domain} config entries with same unique ID

config_entry_unique_id_collision_many.description:
There are multiple ({number_of_entries}) {domain} config entries with the same unique ID.
The first {title_limit} config entries are named {titles}.

To fix this error, [configure the integration]({configure_url}) and remove all except one of the duplicates.

Note: Another group of duplicates may be revealed after removing these duplicates.
config_entry_unique_id_collision_many.title: [%key:component::homeassistant::issues::config_entry_unique_id_collision::title%]

deprecated_trigger_behavior.description:
An automation, script or template entity uses the trigger behavior option `{deprecated_behavior}`, which has been renamed to `{new_behavior}`. The old value still works for now, but support for it will be removed in a future release.

To fix this issue, open each affected automation or script in the editor and save it again; Home Assistant will automatically detect and update the deprecated option. Alternatively, edit your configuration files (for example `automations.yaml`) directly and change `behavior: {deprecated_behavior}` to `behavior: {new_behavior}` in the options of your triggers. Leave the `behavior` option of conditions unchanged, as conditions still use `any` and `all`. Restart Home Assistant afterwards.
deprecated_trigger_behavior.title: Deprecated trigger behavior option in use

deprecated_yaml.description:
Configuring {integration_title} using YAML is being removed.

Your existing YAML configuration has been imported into the UI automatically.

Remove the `{domain}` configuration from your configuration.yaml file and restart Home Assistant to fix this issue.
deprecated_yaml.title: The {integration_title} YAML configuration is being removed

entity_own_area_without_own_name.description:
The entity `{entity_id}` has no name of its own, so it represents its device and is where the device is. An area set on the entity itself contradicts this and is not supported.

To resolve this, open the [entity settings]({entity_settings_url}) and either remove the entity's area or give the entity a name.
entity_own_area_without_own_name.title: Entity {entity_id} has an area but no name of its own

legacy_templates_false.description:
Nothing will change with your templates.

Remove the `legacy_templates` key from the `homeassistant` configuration in your configuration.yaml file and restart Home Assistant to fix this issue.
legacy_templates_false.title: legacy_templates config key is being removed

legacy_templates_true.description:
Please do the following steps:
- Adopt your configuration to support template rendering to native python types.
- Remove the `legacy_templates` key from the `homeassistant` configuration in your configuration.yaml file.
- Restart Home Assistant to fix this issue.
legacy_templates_true.title: The support for legacy templates is being removed

init.description:
There is an ignored orphaned config entry for the `{domain}` integration. This can happen when an integration is removed, but the config entry is still present in Home Assistant.

To resolve this, press **Remove** to clean up the orphaned entry.
init.title: [%key:component::homeassistant::issues::orphaned_ignored_config_entry::title%]

platform_config_not_supported.description:
Configuring the {integration_domain} integration by adding `{platform_key}` under the `{platform_domain}:` key is not supported. The {integration_domain} integration must be configured under its own `{integration_domain}:` key instead.

To resolve this:

1. Remove the following from your YAML configuration file:

{yaml_example}

2. Move the configuration under the `{integration_domain}:` key instead.

3. Restart Home Assistant.

To see the detailed documentation, select Learn more.
platform_config_not_supported.title: Unsupported YAML configuration for the {integration_domain} integration

platform_only.description:
The {domain} integration does not support configuration under its own key, it must be configured under its supported platforms.

To resolve this:

1. Remove `{domain}:` from your YAML configuration file.

2. Restart Home Assistant.
platform_only.title: The {domain} integration does not support YAML configuration under its own key

platform_setup_not_supported.description:
It's not possible to configure {integration_domain} {platform_domain} by adding `{platform_key}` to the {platform_domain} configuration. Please check the documentation for more information on how to set up this integration.

To resolve this:

1. Remove `{platform_key}` occurrences from the `{platform_domain}:` configuration in your YAML configuration file.

2. Restart Home Assistant.
platform_setup_not_supported.title: Unused YAML configuration for the {integration_domain} integration

confirm.description:
The `{storage_key}` storage could not be parsed and has been renamed to `{corrupt_path}` to allow Home Assistant to continue.

A default `{storage_key}` may have been created automatically.

If you made manual edits to the storage file, fix any syntax errors in `{corrupt_path}`, restore the file to the original path `{original_path}`, and restart Home Assistant. Otherwise, restore the system from a backup.

Select **Submit** below to confirm you have repaired the file or restored from a backup.

The exact error was: {error}
confirm.title: [%key:component::homeassistant::issues::storage_corruption::title%]
